mainTopic: Growths on the lung, and needles found in the lung and liver
overview: This amud first finishes two short stories: great sages saw lungs with large growths in the market, some soft and fluid-filled and some hard like rocks, and said nothing to the butchers. Such growths do not make the animal טרפה. Then the גמרא brings a מחלוקת about a needle found in a lung: one group of אמוראים says כשר and another says טרפה. The גמרא explains that the argument is not about whether inside damage counts as חסרון, since everyone agrees it does not. It is about whether the needle came down the airway (כשר) or pierced its way in from the digestive tract (טרפה). In a real case of a needle found in a cut-up lung, רבי אמי finally rules טרפה, because without the whole lung no one can check for a hole. The גמרא settles questions from רב נחמן's rulings, and רב אשי teaches that one טרפה cannot be compared to another. Next comes a needle in the liver: רב אשי says that for a thick needle, we check which way its eye faces to know how it got there, while a thin needle is always assumed to have pierced its way. The amud ends as the גמרא begins comparing this to another found needle, and the comparison continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A sage sees lungs covered with jug-like cysts and says nothing
steps.stepSummary: The end of a story begun before this section: a sage passed through a market and saw lungs full of large fluid-filled cysts, yet did not tell the butchers anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: …of the skinners (some say it was the market of the Sages). He saw those lungs that were full of jug-like bubbles, and he did not say anything at all to the butchers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that started just before this section. A sage saw lungs with big cysts on them and stayed silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His silence is the proof. If these lungs made the animal טרפה, he would have warned the butchers. Since he said nothing, he must have held that such cysts do not make the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The market of the skinners or leather workers
Jug after jug: large fluid-filled cysts or bubbles on the lung

phrases.english: of the skinners, and some say in the market of the Sages,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from the page before: the sage was walking through the skinners' market.

phrases.english: he saw those lungs that were full of jugs upon jugs,
phrases.notes: The 'jugs' are big cysts full of liquid, shaped like little jars.

phrases.english: and he did not say anything at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזֵי הָנָךְ דְּקָיְימָן כַּנְדֵי כַּנְדֵי, וְלָא אָמַר לְהוּ וְלָא מִידֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a story from the previous page about growths on the lung.
steps.raayaObject: That large cysts on the lung do not make the animal טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A great sage's silence when he saw such lungs being sold.

steps.title: רבי אמי and רבי אסי see lungs with hard growths and say nothing
steps.stepSummary: A second story: רבי אמי and רבי אסי passed through the Tiberias market, saw lungs with hard rock-like growths, and did not object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי and רבי אסי were passing through the market of Tiberias. They saw those lungs that were full of rock-like growths, and they did not say anything at all to the butchers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second story with the same message. This time the growths were hard like rocks, and again the sages stayed silent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the first story. Even hard, rock-like growths, not just fluid cysts, did not make רבי אמי and רבי אסי object. So these growths also do not make the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Tiberias, a major city of Torah learning in ארץ ישראל
Rocks upon rocks: hard, stone-like growths on the lung

steps.whatToRemember: Two stories, one message: growths on the lung, whether soft and fluid-filled or hard like rocks, did not lead great sages to call the animal טרפה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
were passing through the market of Tiberias.
They saw those lungs that were full of rocks upon rocks,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'he saw', the word in round brackets. The corrected wording in square brackets says 'they saw', since there are two rabbis.

phrases.english: and they did not say anything at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲווֹ חָלְפִי בְּשׁוּקָא דִּטְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story giving the same kind of proof as step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That hard growths on the lung do not make the animal טרפה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The silence of רבי אמי and רבי אסי in the Tiberias market.

steps.title: Dispute over a needle found inside a lung
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: three אמוראים rule that an animal with a needle found in its lung is כשר, and three others rule it is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: about a needle that was found in the lung, רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי חנינא say the animal is כשר. ריש לקיש, רבי מני בר פטיש and רבי שמעון בן אליקים say it is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It brings a מחלוקת between two groups of three אמוראים about a needle found in a lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling is stated, but no reasons are given yet. The next steps will try to figure out what the two sides are really arguing about.

keyTerms.meaning: They declare it טרפה (a fatally damaged animal, forbidden to eat)

phrases.english: It was stated: a needle that was found in the lung –

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מַכְשְׁרִי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Chanina deem it kosher,
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
and Rabbi Mani bar Pattish
and Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim deem it a tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the lung, separate from the growth stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One group of אמוראים rules כשר and another rules טרפה when a needle is found in the lung.

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue whether inner damage counts as missing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument is about whether damage only on the inside of the lung counts as a חסרון that makes the animal טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about this? One side holds that damage on the inside counts as 'missing', and the other side holds it does not count as 'missing'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a first guess at the root of the מחלוקת. Maybe the needle made a small hole inside the lung, and the question is whether that inner damage counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By this suggestion, both sides agree on the facts: the needle damaged the inside of the lung. Those who say טרפה would hold that inner damage counts as חסרון. Those who say כשר would hold that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: introduces a suggestion that is often rejected
One master holds: refers to one side of the dispute
A deficiency or missing part on the inside of the lung

steps.confusionAlert: Watch for the word לֵימָא ('shall we say'). It is only a suggestion, not the conclusion. The very next step rejects it.

phrases.english: Shall we say they disagree about this:

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר סָבַר: חִסָּרוֹן מִבִּפְנִים – שְׁמֵיהּ חִסָּרוֹן,
phrases.english: that one Sage holds: a deficiency on the inside is called a deficiency,
phrases.notes: This side is the group that says טרפה.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it is not called a deficiency?
phrases.notes: This side is the group that says כשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle the two groups disagree about.

steps.title: Rejection: everyone agrees inner damage does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. All agree that damage only on the inside of the lung is not considered a חסרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that damage on the inside does not count as 'missing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'No' to its own suggestion. Both sides agree that inner damage alone does not make the animal טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This removes the proposed principle from the argument. The מחלוקת must be about something else, and the next step will say what.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees:
a deficiency on the inside is not called a deficiency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion made in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggested explanation of the מחלוקת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no argument about inner damage. All agree it is not a חסרון.

steps.title: The real argument: how did the needle get into the lung?
steps.stepSummary: The groups argue about the needle's path. Did it come down the airway (כשר), or did it pierce its way into the lung from outside (טרפה)?
steps.simpleTranslation: Here they argue about this: one side holds the needle came in through the airway tubes, and the other side holds it pierced its way in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason for the מחלוקת. It is a question of fact about how the needle got into the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those who say כשר assume the needle came through the airways (סמפונות). In that case it only touched the inside of the lung, which everyone agrees does not count. Those who say טרפה assume the needle pierced through from the digestive tract into the lung. That would puncture the lung's outer surface, and a punctured lung makes the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The airway tubes or bronchi leading into the lung
It took that route and came
It surely pierced its way through

steps.whatToRemember: The needle מחלוקת is not about whether inner damage counts, since everyone agrees it does not. It is about the needle's path: through the airway means כשר, and piercing in from outside means טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common move in the גמרא: changing a dispute about a legal principle into a dispute about what probably happened.

phrases.english: And here they disagree about this:
one Sage holds: it took the route of the airway and came in,
phrases.notes: This side says כשר: the needle traveled down the windpipe into the lung's tubes without piercing anything.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: it pierced its way through and came in.
phrases.notes: This side says טרפה: the needle broke through from the food pipe and punctured the lung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the suggestion in step 5, gives the real reason for the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the dispute from a legal principle to a question of fact.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about whether inner damage counts as חסרון.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether the needle came through the airway or pierced its way in.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: כשר if the needle came through the airway. טרפה if it punctured its way into the lung.

steps.title: A needle is found in a cut piece of lung
steps.stepSummary: A real case: a needle was found inside a piece of lung that had already been cut up. It was brought to רבי אמי, who leaned toward ruling it כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a needle found inside a cut-up piece of lung. They brought it to רבי אמי, and he was inclined to rule it כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that puts the needle question from steps 3–6 into practice. This sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The important detail is that the lung was already cut into pieces, so nobody could check the whole lung. רבי אמי's first instinct matches the group from step 3 that rules כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A cut piece (here, a piece of the lung after it was cut up)
To declare it כשר (permitted to eat)

steps.whyThisMatters: The fact that the lung was cut up becomes the key to רבי אמי's final ruling in step 12.

phrases.english: A certain needle that was found
in a cut piece of lung,
they brought it before Rabbi Ami,
he thought to declare it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the needle-in-lung discussion of steps 3–6 to a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי's first inclination: a needle found in a piece of lung is כשר.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה: inside damage counts
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה (or רבי זריקא) objects from the משנה, which lists both 'perforated' and 'missing.' Since 'missing on the outside' would just be a hole, 'missing' must mean on the inside, so inside damage counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה, or some say רבי זריקא, objected: the משנה says 'a lung that was perforated or that was missing' makes the animal טרפה. What does 'missing' mean? If it means missing on the outside, that is the same as a hole! So it must mean missing on the inside. That proves inside damage counts as a real deficiency.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges רבי אמי's leaning toward כשר, using the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is: the משנה would not list two cases that mean the same thing. Outside damage is already covered by 'perforated,' so 'missing' must be adding inside damage. If inside damage makes a טרפה, the needle that damaged the inside of the lung should make it טרפה too.

keyTerms.meaning: It was pierced, has a hole
It is missing a piece, has a deficiency
On the inside / on the outside
And learn from it (a conclusion drawn from a source)

steps.confusionAlert: In step 5 the גמרא said everyone agrees inside damage alone is not a חסרון. This objection argues the opposite. Keep reading: רבי אמי's final ruling in step 12 does not rely on this argument.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya objected to him,
and some say it was Rabbi Zerika:
"The lung that was perforated or that was missing a piece."
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה's list of things that make an animal טרפה.

phrases.english: What does "missing" mean?
If you say missing on the outside, that is the same as perforated!
Rather, doesn't it mean on the inside?
And learn from this:
a deficiency on the inside is considered a deficiency.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי זְרִיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אמי's inclination to rule כשר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's inclination to declare the lung כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word 'חסרה' cannot mean outside damage, which is already 'ניקבה,' so it must mean inside damage. Inside damage therefore makes a טרפה, and the needle caused inside damage.

steps.title: Sent to רבי יצחק נפחא, and the same challenge
steps.stepSummary: The lung is sent to רבי יצחק נפחא, who also leans toward כשר. The same objection from the משנה is raised against him, word for word.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they sent it to רבי יצחק נפחא, and he was also inclined to rule it כשר. רבי ירמיה, or some say רבי זריקא, objected with the same argument: the משנה says 'perforated or missing.' 'Missing' cannot mean on the outside, because that is just a hole. So it must mean on the inside, which shows inside damage counts.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. A second sage leans toward כשר and gets the exact same challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא really does repeat the whole argument, because the objection was actually said a second time to a different sage. Nothing new is added to the argument itself. The point is that the challenge was strong enough that nobody gave a clear ruling of כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him (to him for a ruling)

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: Then they sent it before Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
he thought to declare it kosher,
Rabbi Yirmeya objected to him,
and some say it was Rabbi Zerika:
"The lung that was perforated or that was missing a piece."
What does "missing" mean?
If you say missing on the outside, that is the same as perforated!
Rather, doesn't it mean on the inside?
And learn from this:
a deficiency on the inside is considered a deficiency!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge of step 8 against a second sage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק נפחא's inclination to declare the lung כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same reading of 'חסרה' in the משנה: it must mean inside damage, so inside damage makes a טרפה.

steps.title: Back to רבי אמי, who rules טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The lung is sent back to רבי אמי, and this time he rules it טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they sent it back to רבי אמי, and he ruled it טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The story reaches a ruling: רבי אמי declares the animal טרפה. This sets up the question of how he could disagree with the sages who permitted it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי changed from leaning toward כשר to ruling טרפה. His reason is not given yet; it comes in step 12.

phrases.english: Then they sent it back before Rabbi Ami
and he declared it a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר שַׁדְּרוּהָ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְטַרְפַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sages faced the objection, רבי אמי gives a final ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אמי rules the animal טרפה.

steps.title: But the רבנן permit it
steps.stepSummary: People challenge רבי אמי: the רבנן ruled that an animal with a needle in its lung is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But the רבנן rule that it is כשר!
steps.whatsHappening: People question רבי אמי's ruling of טרפה by pointing to the sages who ruled כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'רבנן' are the three sages from step 3 who ruled that a needle found in the lung is כשר. The question is how רבי אמי can rule against them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the sages (here, the group from step 3 who ruled כשר)

phrases.english: They said to him: But don't the Rabbis declare it kosher?
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" are the three sages back in step 3 who said a needle in the lung is כשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the טרפה ruling of step 10.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Respected sages ruled that a needle in the lung is כשר, so רבי אמי seems to be going against them.

steps.title: They saw the whole lung, and we cannot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers: the sages who permitted knew why they could, since they saw the whole lung. Here the lung is in pieces, and if we had it whole we might find a hole in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: They permitted it because they knew their reason for permitting. But we, on what basis can we permit? Maybe if the whole lung were in front of us, we would see that it was pierced.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי explains that he is not arguing with the רבנן. His case is different, because the lung was cut up and could not be fully checked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן could look at the whole lung and see there was no hole on the outside, which meant the needle came down the airway (as step 6 explained, that is כשר). Here, with only a piece of lung, we cannot rule out that the needle pierced in from the outside, so the animal stays טרפה. This answer is about not knowing the facts, not about whether inside damage counts.

keyTerms.meaning: For what reason, on what basis

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי agrees with the רבנן in principle. He rules טרפה only because the lung was cut up, so no one could check whether the needle pierced in from the outside.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ruling of כשר depends on being able to check the whole lung. Without that, the doubt makes it טרפה.

phrases.english: He said to them: They declared it kosher
because they knew for what reason they declared it kosher,
phrases.notes: They had the whole lung in front of them and could see it had no hole.

phrases.english: but we, for what reason should we declare it kosher?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא אִי הֲוָה רֵיאָה קַמַּן מִינַּקְבָה.
phrases.english: Perhaps if the whole lung were before us, it would turn out to be pierced.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הֵן הִכְשִׁירוּ, שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים מֵאֵיזֶה טַעַם הִכְשִׁירוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the whole lung was available vs. only a cut piece)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אמי is arguing with the רבנן who permitted a needle in the lung.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees with them. He rules טרפה only because the cut-up lung leaves a doubt that it was pierced from outside.

steps.title: But a pierced airway tube is טרפה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that if the whole lung were there and unpierced, it would be כשר. It challenges this from רב נחמן, who says a pierced airway tube (סמפונא) in the lung makes the animal טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he ruled טרפה is that the whole lung was not there. That means if it were there and not pierced, it would be כשר. But רב נחמן said: if an airway tube in the lung is pierced, the animal is טרפה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from רבי אמי's words and then attacks it with a ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the needle came down the airway, it must have poked through the wall of an airway tube to get into the lung tissue. רב נחמן says a pierced airway tube makes a טרפה, so it seems that even a needle that came down the airway should make the animal טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The reason is that it is not here
An airway tube (bronchus) inside the lung

phrases.english: The reason is that the whole lung is not here,
but if it were here and not pierced, it would be kosher.
But didn't Rav Nachman say:
an airway tube of the lung that was pierced makes the animal a tereifa?

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלֵיתַהּ, הָא אִיתַהּ וְלָא מִינַּקְבָה – כְּשֵׁרָה, וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from רבי אמי's answer and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a whole, unpierced lung with a needle that came down the airway is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן rules that a pierced airway tube makes a טרפה, and a needle entering the lung through the airway would pierce such a tube.

steps.title: רב נחמן meant one tube pierced into another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב נחמן's ruling was about an airway tube pierced through into another airway tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ruling of רב נחמן was said about a tube pierced into another tube.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רב נחמן's ruling to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's טרפה is only when the hole goes from one airway tube into another tube. The usual explanation is that the tubes are hard and cannot seal each other's holes, while soft lung tissue around a hole can seal it. So a needle that pierced a tube and went into the soft lung tissue is still כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Into its fellow, into another one (here, into another airway tube)

steps.whatToRemember: A needle that came down the airway into the lung is כשר. רב נחמן's טרפה applies only when one airway tube is pierced into another.

phrases.english: That ruling was said about a tube pierced into another one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רב נחמן in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's rule makes any pierced airway tube a טרפה, including one pierced by a needle that came down the airway.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב נחמן's rule is only about a tube pierced into another tube. A needle that passes from a tube into lung tissue does not make the animal טרפה.

steps.title: Why doesn't one airway tube protect the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 14 from another ruling of רב נחמן: when one coil of the intestine is pierced against another coil, the neighboring coil protects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב נחמן say that if a coil of the colon is pierced right where it touches another coil, the other coil protects it? So why doesn't the neighboring airway tube protect a pierced airway tube too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against the answer in step 14, using a different ruling of רב נחמן about the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said an airway tube pierced into another airway tube makes the animal טרפה. But רב נחמן himself said that with the intestines, a hole facing another coil is 'sealed' by that coil and the animal stays כשר. So why should the lung be any different?

keyTerms.meaning: The spiral colon, the coiled part of the large intestine

phrases.english: But didn't רב נחמן say:
This spiral colon
that was pierced right against its neighbor,
phrases.notes: 'Its neighbor' means the next coil of the intestine that lies pressed up against it.

phrases.english: protects it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 14 by pointing to a similar case with an opposite outcome.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 14 that an airway tube pierced into another airway tube makes the animal טרפה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a neighboring intestine coil seals a hole, a neighboring airway tube should seal one too.

steps.title: You cannot compare one טרפה to another
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that טרפות cannot be compared to each other, because cutting an animal in one spot kills it while cutting in another spot does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Are you comparing טרפות to each other? We do not say about טרפות 'this one is like that one.' You can cut an animal in one place and it dies, and cut it in another place and it lives!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question from step 15 by rejecting the comparison between the intestines and the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of טרפה depend on the exact body part, because each organ reacts to damage differently. So the fact that the intestines can 'seal' a hole tells us nothing about the lung. Each טרפה follows its own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Injuries or defects that make an animal forbidden to eat

keyTerms.term: אֵין אוֹמְרִין בִּטְרֵפוֹת זוֹ דּוֹמָה לָזוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: A rule: with טרפות, we do not learn one case from another

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle in the laws of טרפות: each injury is judged on its own, not by comparing it to a different organ.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Are you comparing טרפות to one another?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִין בִּטְרֵפוֹת זוֹ דּוֹמָה לָזוֹ,
phrases.english: We do not say regarding טרפות: this is similar to that,
for one cuts it here and it dies,
one cuts it there and it lives!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: טְרֵפוֹת קָא מְדַמֵּי לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the comparison between two different body parts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the intestines seal a hole, the lung's airway tubes should too.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each טרפה has its own rule, so the intestine case does not apply to the lung.
steps.whatToRemember: With טרפות, we do not compare one organ to another: a cut in one place kills, while a cut in another place does not.

steps.title: A needle in the main airway of the lung
steps.stepSummary: A needle was found in the main airway of a lung. The strict sages gave no ruling, because the needle may have come in through the breathing passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A needle was found in the main airway of a lung. They brought it to the sages who rule an animal טרפה for a needle in the lung. These sages did not say it was forbidden, and did not say it was permitted. They did not permit it, because of their own view. But they also did not forbid it, because it was found in the main airway, so maybe it went in through the airway and got there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a real case of a needle in the lung, and explains why the strict sages could not decide it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These sages hold that a needle in the lung is usually a sign that it pierced its way there from the digestive tract, which makes the animal טרפה. But a needle in the big main airway may simply have come down the windpipe, with no piercing at all. So they could not forbid it, but their view would not let them permit it either.

keyTerms.meaning: The large, main airway tube of the lung
The sages who rule an animal טרפה when a needle is found in its lung

phrases.english: A certain needle that was found
in the large airway tube of the lung,
they brought it before the sages who forbid,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרוּ בָּהּ לָא אִיסּוּר וְלָא הֶיתֵּר.
phrases.english: they said about it neither forbidden nor permitted.
They did not say it was permitted, in line with their own ruling;
but they also did not say it was forbidden,
since it was found in the large airway tube,
say that it took the path of the airway and came.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא מַחְטָא דְּאִישְׁתְּכַח בְּסִמְפּוֹנָא רַבָּה דְּרֵיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case of a needle in the lung. It shows how the sages from step 3 who rule טרפה deal with a needle found in the main airway, using step 6's idea that a needle may have come down the airway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A needle found in the main airway: the strict sages could not forbid it, since it may have entered through the airway, and they did not permit it.

steps.title: A needle in the liver: מר בריה דרב יוסף wants to forbid
steps.stepSummary: A needle was found in a piece of liver, and מר בריה דרב יוסף thought the animal should be טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A needle was found in a piece of liver. מר, the son of רב יוסף, thought to declare the animal טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case of a needle in the liver and gives one sage's first opinion. This sets up רב אשי's response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר בריה דרב יוסף seems to treat the needle in the liver as a reason to forbid the animal. The next step will question whether a needle in the liver should matter at all.

phrases.english: A certain needle that was found
in a piece of liver,

phrases.aramaic: סְבַר מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְמִיטְרְפַהּ,
phrases.english: מר son of רב יוסף thought to declare it טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new needle case, now in the liver instead of the lung.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בריה דרב יוסף's first view: a needle in the liver makes the animal טרפה.

steps.title: Would you forbid it if the needle were in plain flesh?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges him: if the needle were found the same way in ordinary flesh, would you declare it טרפה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: If a needle had been found like this in ordinary meat, would you, sir, declare it טרפה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes back on מר בריה דרב יוסף's plan to forbid the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole in the liver by itself is like a hole in ordinary flesh: it does not make the animal טרפה. So the needle sitting in the liver is not, on its own, a reason to forbid. The only real question is how it got there.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way, like this

phrases.english: רב אשי said to him:
If it had been found in the flesh in this same way,
would the master declare it טרפה?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִילּוּ אִשְׁתְּכַח בְּבִשְׂרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the view in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר בריה דרב יוסף's plan to forbid because of a needle in the liver
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A hole in the liver is no worse than a hole in ordinary flesh, which does not make an animal טרפה.

steps.title: רב אשי's test: which way does the needle's eye face?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says we look at the needle: if its eye faces out, it pierced its way there; if its eye faces in, it came through a channel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: We look. If the eye of the needle faces outward, it pierced its way and came here. If the eye faces inward, it came through a channel.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the first view, רב אשי gives the correct way to judge the case: check which direction the needle points.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the needle pierced out of the digestive tract to reach the liver, and that piercing would make the animal טרפה. A needle travels point first, so if the eye faces outward, the point went in first from the outside, meaning it came by piercing. If the eye faces inward and the point faces out, it must have traveled through an inner channel, so there was no piercing.

keyTerms.meaning: The eye of the needle (the hole for the thread)

phrases.english: Rather, רב אשי said: We look:
if the eye faces outward,
it pierced its way and came;
phrases.notes: He means it pierced out of the digestive tract to get to the liver, which makes the animal טרפה.

phrases.english: if the eye faces inward,
it took the path of a channel and came.
phrases.notes: Here סמפונא means a blood vessel inside the liver, not an airway tube like in the lung.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected view from step 18 with the correct method.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eye facing outward: it pierced its way, so טרפה. Eye facing inward: it came through a channel, so כשר.
steps.confusionAlert: The liver hole itself is never the problem. The question is only whether the needle pierced the digestive tract on its way to the liver.

steps.title: The test only works for a thick needle
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי's test applies only to a thick needle. A thin needle is assumed to have pierced its way, no matter which way it faces.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only to a thick needle. But with a thin needle, it makes no difference whether the eye faces in or out: it pierced its way and came.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב אשי's test from step 20 to thick needles only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thick needle's eye end is too blunt to pierce, so if the eye faces outward we know the point did the piercing, and if it faces inward it must have come through a channel. A thin needle is sharp enough at either end to pierce, so its direction proves nothing. We assume it pierced, and the animal is טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: And these words apply (only) to..., introduces a limit on a rule

steps.whatToRemember: Needle in the liver: with a thick needle, eye outward means טרפה and eye inward means כשר. With a thin needle, it is always assumed to have pierced its way, so it is טרפה.

phrases.english: And this applies to a thick one;
but a thin one,
no difference if the eye faces inward,
no difference if the eye faces outward,
it pierced its way and came.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the test in step 20 to thick needles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thin needle in the liver is always assumed to have pierced its way there, whichever way it faces.

steps.title: How is this different from another found needle?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask why the needle rules just taught are different from another case of a needle that was found.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this case different from a needle that is found...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It starts to compare our needle case to another needle case, and the rest of the question comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words מאי שנא mean 'what is the difference?' They are used when two cases look alike but seem to be treated differently. The גמרא is about to point to another found needle whose ruling seems to clash with the rules in steps 20–21. The other case and the answer come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference? A phrase that asks why two cases that look alike get different rulings

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Don't try to work out the answer yet. The גמרא still has to tell us where the other needle was found.

phrases.english: And what is different
from a needle that is found

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the needle rules from steps 20–21 by comparing them to another case of a found needle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rules about whether a needle pierced its way in or came through a natural channel (steps 20–21)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two needle cases seem alike, so they should get the same ruling. The גמרא asks what makes them different. The full comparison continues in the next lines.
